reason: An info-only finding that is also wrong against the pre-registered timing, so it would mislead if logged. (1) It computes 'latest useful submit' as 20:00Z tick minus L, giving 10:30Z for CI and 12:45Z for non-CI. The registered rule CONTEXT l.3171-3176, (7) LAST USEFUL SUBMIT, anchors on 18:30Z instead: T_last = 18:30Z - (L_ref + 0.25 h), which is about 10:25-10:30Z and never later than 11:00Z. CI files get T_last - 2.4 h, about 08:05Z. The rule also says 'a file submitted after its T_last is never a finals candidate'. The FINALS READ is ~19:00Z (l.3194, l.3376), and the user must decide before ticking. An E10 copy submitted between 10:30Z and 12:45Z under this reminder would break rule (7), and a CI-like copy sent at 10:30Z would miss the 19:00Z finals read. (2) After 02:00Z the E10 edge is already written down: an E10 copy is allowed until about 10:00Z, only on the user's yes for that notebook (l.3376, l.3612-3614). The cap lift covers up to 2 NON-CI files until about 10:25Z (l.3606). After 02:00Z no CI file goes without the user's explicit yes (l.3394). (3) The finding ignores the slot budget. Probes 52-54 used 3 of the 5 29-Sep slots, and the remaining 2 belong to MORNING TABLE v1.1 (A-M1 exp89l by 08:45Z, A-M2 by 11:30Z). An E10 copy would displace one of them, which the finding does not mention. (4) Labelling a public notebook 'CI-like' or 'non-CI-like' has no basis. Its runtime is its own and has no ledger entry, so L_hi (and V_pub eligibility, which needs L_hi <= 9.0 h non-CI or <= 10.75 h CI on a COMPLETE ref) is unknown until it is read. (5) The trigger is now >= 0.960, since exp87a read 0.959 (l.4175-4199). The finding's note '0.960+ after ~11:00Z = information only' is consistent, but its cutoff times are not. The claim that watch_loop.log runs 'until 2026-09-29T12:00:00Z' is correct. No private value, no LB value.
fix: Do not log the 10:30Z / 12:45Z arithmetic. If a reminder is wanted, restate the existing rules instead. An E10 copy after 02:00Z needs (a) a notebook whose own public score is >= 0.960, (b) build and a PASSED dummy, (c) the user's yes for that notebook, and (d) a submit by ~10:00Z (non-CI hard T_last ~10:25-10:30Z = 18:30Z - (L_hi + 0.25 h); CI only on explicit yes, T_last ~08:05Z). It takes one of the 2 remaining 29-Sep slots ahead of A-M2, and ahead of A-M1 only if the user says so. Any >= 0.960 notebook seen after ~09:30Z (too late for build + dummy + yes by 10:00Z) is information for the user only, never a finals candidate.
